related_questions.question: What are the symptoms of Covid-19 in the digestive system?

text_blocks.snippet: Digestive symptoms are common in COVID-19 infections, with about 50% of people experiencing them. These symptoms can include nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. They may be an early sign of infection or develop later, and they can also persist as part of long COVID. The virus's ability to target ACE2 receptors in the gut, along with the presence of viral RNA in feces, may contribute to these gastrointestinal issues.

text_blocks.snippet: Gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms can be part of long COVID, with some individuals experiencing long-lasting gut issues after a COVID-19 infection. These symptoms can include upper abdominal pain, bloating, and changes in bowel movements.
snippet_highlighted_words: upper abdominal pain, bloating, and changes in bowel movements

text_blocks.snippet: Specific GI symptoms associated with long COVID may include:

list.snippet: Abdominal pain: Upper abdominal pain is a common complaint.
Bloating: Feeling of fullness or swelling in the abdomen.
Changes in bowel movements: This could involve diarrhea, constipation, or other alterations in bowel habits.
Other potential symptoms: Yale Medicine articles suggest some patients may experience a range of other GI issues, potentially linked to microbiome changes.
The exact mechanisms of how COVID-19 might affect the gut are still being researched.
Some studies suggest a link between long COVID GI symptoms and microbiome changes.

If you are experiencing persistent gut problems after a COVID-19 infection, it's crucial to consult with your doctor to rule out other potential causes and discuss possible treatment options, including those that may help with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) as suggested by Harvard Health.
